editorial.headline: Post-Production’s Open National Market, and Bali’s Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: This private post-production activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but in Bali the exact scope declared in OSS determines whether PMA registration is possible.
editorial.body:
Film, video, audiovisual works and television programmes reach their finished form in post-production. This private-sector activity covers the work that happens after production: editing and cutting; dubbing; titles and film credits; closed captioning; animation and special effects; film or tape transfer; and conversion into video-streaming formats. It also includes film studios and specialist animation-film studios that develop and process films, reproduce them for cinema distribution, and manage paid documentation or stock-footage services.

The scope extends to privately managed post-production involving sports-media content, as well as film, video and television censorship performed by a business entity or business actor as part of the post-production process. In practical terms, this is a broad operational category for the businesses responsible for shaping, adapting, processing and preparing moving-image material for its intended distribution. The record also carries a specific qualifier concerning animation, so the exact activity declared matters as much as the general post-production description.

Nationally, the position is straightforward: the activity is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. It is available across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That national openness, however, should not be mistaken for an automatic Bali registration outcome. Bali’s permanent province-wide rule blocks all Low- and Medium-Low-risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. For this activity at the Besar scale, the OSS risk result is low for some scopes and higher for others.

That distinction is the whole Bali story. The activity is not recorded as outright blocked, but PMA registration in Bali is possible only when the declaration uses the higher-risk scope. A founder cannot safely rely on the national 100% ceiling alone, nor on the generic label of post-production. The exact activity must be checked in live OSS before registration, because the Bali result depends on the scope selected rather than on a blanket provincial approval or refusal.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is not a Bali registration answer: eligibility turns on the exact scope declared in OSS.
